| Wald test of nested linear models (`waldtest`; `validation/regression/regression_legacy_cases.md`) | lmtest::waldtest(test = 'F' \| 'Chisq'); aod::wald.test (legacy reference, equal to the Chisq form) | `diag_wald_sim`, `ols_diagnostics_grunfeld` | F statistic, df1, df2, F p-value, RSS of both models, parameter counts, n | validation/README.md, n = 100 and 200: statistics and RSS 1e-6 relative; p-values 1e-6 relative or 1e-12 absolute; counts exact | `p2a-core::regression::diagnostics::tests::test_validate_wald_sim`<br>`p2a-core::regression::diagnostics::tests::test_validate_wald_grunfeld` | PASS (known deviations) |

### Known deviations

- `driscoll_kraay`: REG-24, Driscoll-Kraay SEs, covariance, t and p: scores are averaged within period and the meat is multiplied by T: p2a 0.02186774128 / 0.04533713058 = sqrt(T)/N (0.4472135955) x vcovPL 0.04889775602 / 0.1013769059 (vcovpl_lag2 = vcovscc_lag2). The legacy reference vcovPL(cluster = ~time, order.by = ~time) aggregates by firm, not period (legacy_vcovpl_cluster_time), and is not a Driscoll-Kraay value
- `driscoll_kraay`: REG-50, non-Bartlett kernels: Parzen, Tukey-Hanning and QS use the j/m bandwidth convention while vcovPL uses bw = lag + 1; not pinned, and no case holds a vcovPL value for them, so there is no R or p2a value to record
- `gls`: REG-43, estimated rho ('ar1_auto') and the fit that uses it: the lag-1 correlation of the OLS residuals, 0.6541921822, not nlme's REML 0.6819761522 (phi) or ML 0.6532503857 (phi_ml)
- `gls`: REG-9, log-likelihood, AIC, BIC: omit -0.5 log\|Omega\| and use SSE/(n - p): at phi p2a gives -93.62614993, AIC 193.2522999, BIC 198.9883689 (post Tier 0) vs nlme REML logLik -79.12921201, AIC 166.2584240, BIC 173.7432281
- `hac`: REG-50, Quadratic Spectral SEs: the QS kernel is truncated at the bandwidth: p2a 0.2284575999 / 0.1414513262 vs kernHAC(kernel = 'Quadratic Spectral', bw = 4, prewhite = FALSE, adjust = FALSE) 0.2300539548 / 0.1392422079 (kernhac_qs_bw4)
- `hac`: REG-50, Bartlett bandwidth convention: p2a's Bartlett bandwidth m weights lag j by 1 - j/(m + 1), i.e. NeweyWest(lag = m) = kernHAC(bw = m + 1) (pinned); kernHAC(kernel = 'Bartlett', bw = 4) is 0.2102028704 / 0.1464461033 (kernhac_bartlett_bw4) where p2a's m = 4 gives 0.2204664393 / 0.1429954779. Parzen, Truncated and Tukey-Hanning use j/m and match kernHAC(bw = m)
- `hac`: REG-22, prewhitened SEs: prewhiten = true fits a scalar AR(1) to the residuals: p2a 0.2908704449 / 0.3059566437 vs NeweyWest(lag = 4, prewhite = TRUE) 0.2858936714 / 0.1360607244 (neweywest_lag4_prewhite)
- `hac`: REG-61, default bandwidth and small-sample adjustment: the default bandwidth is the fixed rule floor(4 (n/100)^(2/9)) = 4, not bwNeweyWest (2.513298742, bw_neweywest); there is no adjust = TRUE option: kernhac_*_bw4_adjust hold the adjusted values, e.g. Parzen 0.1977403619 / 0.1432982597 where p2a gives the unadjusted 0.1957529711 / 0.1418580397
- `ordered_newton_many_categories`: ECON-4, coefficients, thresholds and log-likelihood (logit and probit): the beta score has the wrong sign and the outer-product Hessian divides by p_i twice, so the fit never reaches polr's MLE (converged = false after 100 iterations); T2-WP10 pins logit_*/probit_* of these cases
- `ordered_newton_many_categories`: ECON-5, standard errors: hard-coded 0.1; T2-WP10 computes them from the observed information
- `quantreg`: REG-52, coefficients: IRLS with an absolute 1e-4 weight cap approximates the LP solution: relative differences from rq of 1.8e-5 / 5.5e-8 (tau 0.25), 2.8e-5 / 7.7e-6 (0.5), 1.0e-6 / 1.8e-6 (0.75) against the 1e-8 coefficient tolerance; tau 0.5 p2a 1.348696693 / 3.169975618 vs rq 1.348734984 / 3.169951199 (coef_tau50); the objective is within 2.3e-7 of rq's minimum
- `quantreg`: REG-26, standard errors, t, p: about sqrt(n) too small and an iid Silverman/Epanechnikov sparsity: tau 0.5 p2a 0.05028920546 / 0.008320075224 vs summary.rq iid 0.4807247768 / 0.07953329683, nid 0.1798711171 / 0.1079530876
- `quantreg`: REG-64, 95% confidence intervals: use 1.96 instead of a t quantile, around the REG-26 SEs: tau 0.5 slope p2a 3.153668270 to 3.186282965, i.e. estimate +/- 1.96 x 0.008320075224, where a t(98) interval on the same SE would use 1.984467455; no case holds an R interval (summary.rq's default rank-inversion intervals are not recorded)
- `resettest`: REG-35, type = 'princomp': not implemented: ResetType::PrinComp reuses the fitted-value augmentation; not exercised by any case. On Grunfeld (inv ~ value + capital, powers 2:3) p2a gives the fitted F 19.56011807 where resettest(type = 'princomp') gives 6.108133142 (df 2, 195)
- `waldtest`: REG-37, Chisq statistic and p-value: p2a uses n (RSS_r - RSS_u) / RSS_u; lmtest::waldtest(test = 'Chisq') and aod::wald.test give q F = (n - k) (RSS_r - RSS_u) / RSS_u: diag_wald_sim drop x2 0.01248835701 vs 0.01198882273, drop x2 and x3 514.9909496 vs 494.3913116; Grunfeld drop capital 83.23811806 vs 81.98954629
